decisions.reason: As a low-cost extension of the core bread range with no clear negative signal yet, it still has option value despite overlap with other rye breads.
The product is a stated flagship and its gold-medal recognition is strong evidence of realized value, so management would very likely continue backing it.
This seeded rye mixed bread is close to existing capabilities and cheap to carry, so the firm is likely to keep it while demand becomes clearer, though portfolio crowding raises its risk somewhat.
Because it is another nearby rye variant in a fairly full launch set, it faces some substitution risk, but absent poor performance evidence the option is still worth keeping for now.
A marzipan stollen fits the firm's seasonal confectionery strengths and can be retained at limited incremental cost, even if it is less central than the premium raisin flagship.
The ancient grain bread is a recent differentiated launch with uncertain upside, and real-options logic favors keeping such a product when the downside of waiting is modest.
